A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, Towards Robust Influence Functions with Flat Validation Minima. All 21 pages of each, including figures, tables, equations and Appendices A–G, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments on mislabeled-sample detection, relabeling, and influential-sample identification in text and image generation, plus ablations and appendix analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results in Section 4 and Appendix C. Results retained from v1 still qualify as original empirical outcomes.

M1.justification: The VM/FVM procedures, validation-minimum optimization, second-order influence estimator and diagonal Fisher approximation remain unchanged in Section 3 and Appendix A.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same CIFAR-10N/100N detection and relabeling tasks, sentence transformations, arithmetic problems, and image style/subject generation datasets and scenarios.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain LiSSA/LiSSA*, TracIn, GEX, DataInf/DataInf* and the appendix EK-FAC/EK-FAC* comparisons. Table 3's change from TM to VM corrects a label rather than introducing a comparator.

E3.justification: Sections 4 and B retain the same splits, sample sizes, metrics, model configurations, training budgets and checkpoint-selection procedures. The appendix evaluation settings also remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The component ablation in Table 6 and analyses of validation-set size, sharpness-aware optimizers and inverse-Hessian approximations in Appendix C are all retained without substantive revision.

E5.justification: Both versions retain three-run mean±standard-deviation reporting for the same experiments, variation across validation samples for generation metrics, and five random vectors for the Appendix C.4 approximation.

E6.justification: Numerical results and plotted findings are unchanged throughout the main text and appendices. Table 3 retains 58.13±0.15 and 70.61±0.24; changing TM to VM only corrects the method label.

T1.justification: Definition 3.1, Theorem 3.2, Corollary 3.3 and the proofs and derivations in Appendices D–E are mathematically unchanged. Newly calling the definition and corollary 'Theorem' in cross-references does not revise their substance.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about validation-risk sharpness, influence-estimation error, the proposed estimator and its experimental advantages.

C2.justification: Explanations involving vanishing gradients and parameter-change misalignment remain unchanged, as do qualifications concerning optimization cost, simplified LPF settings and inverse-Hessian approximation performance.

D1.justification: The introduction changes the IF-FVM code-repository account from Virusdol to Virusdoll, including the hyperlink destination. Implementation and hyperparameter disclosures are otherwise unchanged. The PDFs do not establish whether either address works.

R1.justification: The cited works, bibliography and research positioning in Appendix F are unchanged, including the claimed gap concerning validation-risk sharpness.

P1.justification: Limited edits update metadata and cross-reference wording, including Appendix to Section. References to Definition 3.1 and Corollary 3.3 incorrectly become Theorem references. The narrative and section organization remain substantially unchanged.

P2.justification: Table 3 corrects TM to VM, and Table 9 moves from page 15 to page 14 with associated reflow. The figures and remaining table structures are retained; no new displays are introduced.

improvement.justification: Scientific content and evidence are unchanged. Correcting Table 3's method label improves clarity, but v2 introduces incorrect theorem cross-references. Its changed code address could affect reproducibility, yet the PDFs cannot establish the effect on access. These mixed, limited edits leave the overall direction of quality change uncertain.
